The disjointness this rests on is fixed by the closed set `listLiveNegotiationFiles` reports — `RECOVERY_NEGOTIATION_FILENAMES` (`src/preserve-work-recovery.ts:828-834`: `context.md`, `contract-review.json`, `contract-response.json`, `contract-negotiation-outcome.json`, `planner-escalation.md`) plus every `feedback-r<N>.md` round (`:847-860`) — which contains neither `CONTRACT_FILENAME` nor `ACCEPTANCE_MANIFEST_FILENAME`

behaviors.given: four families of input. (a) A forced restore failure — an unwritable destination, and separately a snapshot file removed. (b) A well-formed persisted `ROLLBACK_FAILED` event. (c) A persisted `ROLLBACK_FAILED` event that is missing `rollbackError`, and again with it present but blank, and again for each of `observedContractFingerprint` and `observedManifestFingerprint`. (d) A persisted `PENDING` event carrying `rollbackError`, and a persisted `ROLLED_BACK` event carrying `observedContractFingerprint`
behaviors.when: for (a) `rollBackRecoveryAttempt` runs; for (b), (c) and (d) the state file is saved and loaded back through `sanitizeRecoveryLineage`
behaviors.then: for (a) it appends exactly one `ROLLBACK_FAILED` event carrying the trailing `PENDING` event's `attemptId` verbatim plus the failure message and the fingerprints observed on disk (an absent file recorded as an explicit absent marker, not a blank), appends no `ROLLED_BACK`, and claims no rollback in its result. The observed facts ride three new **optional** fields — `rollbackError`, `observedContractFingerprint`, `observedManifestFingerprint` — required non-blank when `state` is `ROLLBACK_FAILED` and required absent otherwise, with no `RUN_STATE_VERSION` bump, on the `specsDir` precedent. Because that rule changes the validator's accepted input language, both halves of its regression surface are bound per ADR 0060: (b) loads unchanged, while (c) and (d) are each rejected — a rule enforced in one direction only would still pass every accepted-input test
behaviors.observableResult: a test named `[behavior:#333:B-06]` in `src/preserve-work-recovery.test.ts` asserts, for each forced failure, that the lineage grew by exactly one `ROLLBACK_FAILED` event whose `attemptId` equals the `PENDING` event's, whose `rollbackError` is the failure message, whose `observedContractFingerprint`/`observedManifestFingerprint` are the values actually read from disk (with the explicit absent marker for a missing file), that no `ROLLED_BACK` exists for the attempt, and that the event round-trips through save/load. Tests named `[behavior:#333:B-06]` in `src/run-state.test.ts` bind the rejections inline, as that file's established harness: for each of the eight (c) variants — missing and blank, for each of the three fields — and for each (d) variant, loading the file leaves the target's whole lineage list absent, taking the pre-existing degrade-to-absent consequence at `src/run-state.ts:1140-1141,1160` unchanged. Each rejection test asserts the same document loads intact once the offending field is corrected or removed, so it cannot pass because of an unrelated malformation

behaviors.given: run state whose lineage for the target ends on `ROLLBACK_FAILED`, and separately state whose lineage ends on `PENDING`, on `ROLLED_BACK`, and on `COMPLETED`

It is exported for #334; this slice wires it into no orchestrator or dispatch call site
behaviors.observableResult: a test named `[behavior:#333:B-07]` asserts the returned message contains the exact `attemptId` and `snapshotPath` strings taken from the trailing event, and asserts `undefined` for the `PENDING`, `ROLLED_BACK` and `COMPLETED` cases. A second assertion greps the diff-visible import graph to confirm no module outside `src/preserve-work-recovery.ts` and its test file imports the export

behaviors.given: a target whose lineage ends on `ROLLBACK_FAILED` and whose restore obstacle has since been removed

behaviors.then: the retry restores and verifies from the same snapshot and appends `ROLLED_BACK` carrying that same event's `attemptId` — the rule `PersistedRecoveryLineageEvent`'s own doc comment already fixes (`src/run-state.ts:269-277`: every terminal event is a new record citing the same `attemptId`, nothing edits or deletes an earlier one, so a retry is always a fresh attempt ID); every other outbound transition from `ROLLBACK_FAILED` is refused by the unedited `LEGAL_RECOVERY_TRANSITIONS`, no path appends a second `PENDING` for an existing attempt, and no existing event is edited or deleted
behaviors.observableResult: a test named `[behavior:#333:B-08]` asserts the appended `ROLLED_BACK` event's `attemptId` is string-equal to the `ROLLBACK_FAILED` event's, asserts every earlier event is still present byte-for-byte at its original index in the append-only list, asserts each non-`ROLLED_BACK` outbound transition from `ROLLBACK_FAILED` is refused, and asserts a fresh admission afterwards produces an event whose `attemptId` differs from that one and whose `snapshotPath` names a different directory

A second, independent compare inside the writer could not keep that identity true, so one induced obstacle producing the identically-shaped failure through both entry points is the mechanical form of the single-implementation obligation
